concepts.name: ASEAN's Founding: Bangkok Declaration (1967) and Original Members
key_dimensions: Five founding members (Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand) vs. current 10 members — UPSC trap: confusing founding vs. current members
Cold War geopolitical context and anti-communist motivation vs. stated economic cooperation purpose
Distinction from later joiners: Brunei (1984), Vietnam (1995), Laos & Myanmar (1997), Cambodia (1999)
ASEAN's expansion logic: CLMV countries joining post-Cold War and implications for development disparity within bloc

concepts.name: ASEAN Charter (2007): Legal Personality and Institutional Reform
key_dimensions: Significance of granting ASEAN a legal personality — first time, enabling it to sign treaties as a body
Shift from loose intergovernmental forum to rules-based organization with binding commitments
Key organs created/formalized: ASEAN Summit, ASEAN Coordinating Council, ASEAN Community Councils
UPSC trap: Charter did NOT make ASEAN a supranational body like the EU — sovereignty principle retained

concepts.name: ASEAN Way: Principle of Non-Interference and Consensus Decision-Making
key_dimensions: Core principles: non-interference in internal affairs, consensus-based decisions, informality over legalism
Criticism: 'ASEAN Way' as obstacle to resolving Myanmar coup crisis, South China Sea disputes
Contrast with EU's supranational enforcement mechanism — UPSC frequently tests this comparison
ASEAN's inability to expel or sanction members as a structural limitation (no Article 7-equivalent)

concepts.name: ASEAN Community 2015: Three Pillars Structure
key_dimensions: Three pillars: ASEAN Political-Security Community (APSC), ASEAN Economic Community (AEC), ASEAN Socio-Cultural Community (ASCC)
UPSC trap: AEC is NOT a customs union or common market — it is a single market and production base with nuanced differences
Bali Concord II (2003) as foundational document for the three-community vision
Progress gap: AEC declared in 2015 but non-tariff barriers, service sector integration remain incomplete

concepts.name: ASEAN Economic Community (AEC): Goals, Achievements, and Limitations
key_dimensions: Four characteristics: single market & production base, competitive economic region, equitable economic development, integration into global economy
ASEAN Free Trade Area (AFTA) and CEPT scheme as precursor — tariffs reduced to 0-5% among ASEAN-6
UPSC trap: AEC ≠ Common Market (no free movement of all labor; only skilled labor under Mutual Recognition Arrangements)
Key limitation: CLMV countries given longer transition timelines, creating a two-speed ASEAN

concepts.name: ASEAN Free Trade Area (AFTA) and CEPT/ATIGA Mechanism
key_dimensions: AFTA established 1992; Common Effective Preferential Tariff (CEPT) scheme as original instrument
CEPT replaced by ASEAN Trade in Goods Agreement (ATIGA) in 2010 — more comprehensive and legally binding
Inclusion lists vs. exclusion lists (General Exceptions, Sensitive List, Highly Sensitive List for agriculture)
UPSC trap: AFTA is NOT a customs union — no common external tariff; each member retains its own tariff for non-ASEAN trade

concepts.name: RCEP: ASEAN-Centrality in the World's Largest Trade Bloc
key_dimensions: RCEP signed November 2020; covers 15 countries (ASEAN-10 + China, Japan, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand)
India's withdrawal in 2019 — concerns over trade deficit with China, dairy and agricultural sector vulnerability
ASEAN centrality principle: ASEAN as the hub/convener, not China or any external power
UPSC trap: RCEP is NOT an ASEAN agreement — it is a separate treaty where ASEAN is the convening body; India is NOT a member

concepts.name: ASEAN+3 and ASEAN+6: Dialogue Partner Architecture
key_dimensions: ASEAN+3: ASEAN plus China, Japan, South Korea — emerged from 1997 Asian financial crisis
Chiang Mai Initiative (CMI) and its multilateralization (CMIM) as key financial safety net born from ASEAN+3
ASEAN+6 (East Asia Summit format): adds India, Australia, New Zealand; later US and Russia
UPSC trap: Distinguishing ASEAN+3, ASEAN+6, EAS, and ARF — overlapping memberships cause frequent confusion

concepts.name: India–ASEAN Relations: Strategic Partnership and Trade Agreement
key_dimensions: India became ASEAN's Dialogue Partner in 1992, Summit-level partner in 2002, Strategic Partner in 2012
ASEAN–India Free Trade Agreement (AIFTA) in goods signed 2009, entered force 2010; services & investment FTA signed 2015
Act East Policy (2014) as upgrade of Look East Policy — ASEAN as its cornerstone
UPSC trap: India is a Dialogue Partner, NOT a member of ASEAN; also distinguish India's role in EAS vs. ARF vs. ADMM+

concepts.name: ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF): Security Architecture
key_dimensions: ARF established 1994 — ASEAN's premier security dialogue forum with 27 members including US, China, India, EU
Three-stage process: confidence building → preventive diplomacy → conflict resolution (stage 3 never reached)
UPSC trap: ARF is a dialogue forum, NOT a military alliance or collective security arrangement
Distinction from ADMM+ (ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting Plus) which is defence-specific and has only 18 members

concepts.name: ASEAN's South China Sea Position: DOC vs. COC
key_dimensions: Declaration on Conduct of Parties (DOC) 2002 — non-binding political document between ASEAN and China
Code of Conduct (COC) negotiations ongoing since 2017 — legally binding instrument being negotiated
ASEAN disunity trap: Cambodia and Laos (Chinese influence) historically blocked ASEAN consensus on SCS language
UNCLOS as legal framework — ASEAN members use it; China's nine-dash line vs. 2016 Arbitral Tribunal ruling (which China rejects)

concepts.name: Chiang Mai Initiative Multilateralization (CMIM): ASEAN's Financial Safety Net
key_dimensions: Origin: 1997–98 Asian Financial Crisis exposed lack of regional financial safety net
CMI (2000) → CMIM (2010): multilateral currency swap arrangement worth $240 billion
AMRO (ASEAN+3 Macroeconomic Research Office) as surveillance body for CMIM — established 2011
UPSC trap: CMIM is linked to IMF — countries can access only 40% of quota without an IMF program (IMF de-linkage threshold raised but IMF conditionality still relevant)

concepts.name: ASEAN's Institutional Structure: Summit, Secretariat, and Committees
key_dimensions: ASEAN Summit is the supreme decision-making body — meets twice a year (post-Charter formalization)
ASEAN Secretariat located in Jakarta, Indonesia — headed by Secretary-General (5-year term, one per country on rotation)
UPSC trap: ASEAN has no legislative body, no court of justice, and no enforcement mechanism — unlike EU
ASEAN Intergovernmental Commission on Human Rights (AICHR) — consultative only, no binding power; contrast with EU's ECHR

concepts.name: ASEAN Connectivity: Master Plan on ASEAN Connectivity (MPAC)
key_dimensions: MPAC 2010 and updated MPAC 2025 — covers physical, institutional, and people-to-people connectivity
Key projects: ASEAN Highway Network, Singapore-Kunming Rail Link (SKRL) — still incomplete
India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway as India's connectivity link to ASEAN under Act East Policy
UPSC trap: SKRL passes through Myanmar — political instability post-2021 coup has stalled progress; India's Kaladan project also affected

concepts.name: ASEAN's Engagement with Major Powers: US, China, Japan Comparative Dynamics
key_dimensions: US–ASEAN: Indo-Pacific Strategy, IPEF (India-Pacific Economic Framework) as US's economic re-engagement tool post-TPP withdrawal
China–ASEAN: Largest trading partner since 2009; BRI projects in mainland ASEAN; debt diplomacy concerns
Japan–ASEAN: Fukuda Doctrine (1977) as foundational — heart-to-heart diplomacy; Japan a major ODA provider
UPSC trap: IPEF is NOT a free trade agreement — no market access commitments; contrast with RCEP which has tariff schedules

concepts.name: ASEAN's Response to Myanmar Crisis (2021): Five-Point Consensus
key_dimensions: Five-Point Consensus (April 2021): cessation of violence, dialogue, humanitarian aid, special envoy, envoy visit to Myanmar
ASEAN's non-interference principle vs. pressure to act — structural tension exposed
Myanmar's junta representative barred from ASEAN Summits (unprecedented step) but Myanmar not expelled
UPSC angle: Tests understanding of limits of 'ASEAN Way' and whether ASEAN can evolve its norms under pressure

concepts.name: ASEAN's Trade and Economic Statistics: Key Data Points for Prelims
key_dimensions: ASEAN's combined GDP: ~$3.6 trillion (5th largest economy if treated as single entity); growing to 4th by 2030 projections
ASEAN is India's 4th largest trading partner and India is ASEAN's 7th largest; bilateral trade ~$130 billion
Intra-ASEAN trade as share of total ASEAN trade: ~25% — relatively low, indicating limited internal integration vs. EU (~60%)
UPSC trap: Frequently tested — China is ASEAN's largest external trading partner, NOT the US or Japan

concepts.name: ASEAN's Role in Indo-Pacific: ASEAN Outlook on the Indo-Pacific (AOIP)
key_dimensions: AOIP adopted 2019 — ASEAN's own vision for Indo-Pacific emphasizing inclusivity, ASEAN centrality, and non-alignment
Distinguishes ASEAN's approach from Quad's Indo-Pacific (security-focused) and China's rejection of Indo-Pacific framing
Four areas of cooperation under AOIP: maritime cooperation, connectivity, SDGs, economic cooperation
UPSC trap: AOIP explicitly avoids military alliance framing — it is a cooperative, not confrontational, Indo-Pacific vision; India must engage ASEAN through AOIP lens

concepts.name: ASEAN's Preferential Trade Agreements with External Partners: Comparative Overview
key_dimensions: ASEAN FTAs: ASEAN-China FTA (2005), ASEAN-Korea FTA (2007), ASEAN-Japan CEPA (2008), ASEAN-India FTA (2010), ASEAN-Australia-NZ FTA (2010), ASEAN-Hong Kong FTA (2019)
UPSC trap: ASEAN-India FTA covers only goods (signed 2009) — services and investment FTA is a separate agreement (2015); review of goods FTA ongoing
India's concerns: Trade deficit widened post-AIFTA; demand to upgrade/renegotiate the goods FTA
Contrast: ASEAN-China FTA has led to Chinese goods flooding ASEAN markets — similar concern India raised for itself

concepts.name: ASEAN and Sustainable Development: Blue Economy, Digital Economy, and Green Transition
key_dimensions: ASEAN Comprehensive Recovery Framework (ACRF) 2020 — COVID-19 recovery blueprint with green and digital economy pillars
ASEAN Digital Masterplan 2025: digital connectivity, digital payments (Project Nexus linking payment systems), cybersecurity
ASEAN Blue Economy Framework — maritime Southeast Asia's dependence on ocean resources and SCS overlap
UPSC angle: ASEAN-India Digital Work Plan and UPI's potential expansion to ASEAN as India's soft power in digital payments
